body:
The complete original and supplement for Robshaw et al. (2020), [DOI 10.1007/s12649-020-00954-1](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12649-020-00954-1), support laboratory chemical leaching and resin separation from real mixed-cut spent potlining. This source follow-up concerns unresolved experimental details; the qualified record does not claim an optimized transferable recipe, an overall feed-to-product yield or industrial deployment.

The acquired institutional originals contain these differences:

- Experimental, “Leaching Treatment of SPL” (article page 4; repository PDF page 5), describes 250 mL 0.5 M sulfuric acid for 3 h. Figure 4b and its caption (article page 9; PDF page 10) specify 1 M acid; SI Table S2 (numbered page 13; repository PDF page 14) specifies 0.5 M and an acid-stage duration of 2 h.
- Experimental, “Fluoride Uptake by La-MTS9501 and Elution in Fixed-Bed Column Studies” (article page 4; PDF page 5), states 1.00 bed volume/h. Main Figures 5–6 and SI Figure S33 specify 0.50 bed volume/h.
- The reported 59.0% fluoride recovery is calculated from the main elution-peak area divided by model-derived theoretical column uptake, not an original waste inventory. Early water-wash losses, impure precipitation during leachate mixing and a complete feed-to-product mass balance need separate accounting. Main Figure 6/Table 5 show a multicomponent eluate; pure final cryolite precipitation was future work.

Acceptance work:

1. Obtain a legitimate correction, raw experiment record or other citable primary clarification linking exact acid concentration, contact time and flow rate to each plotted arm. Do not silently select whichever source statement looks plausible.
2. Reconcile model capacity, loading, wash, elution and mixing-loss inventories and their uncertainty before accepting an overall recovery percentage. Distinguish measurement replicates from independent leach/column campaigns.
3. If evaluating later studies such as [DOI 10.1016/j.clpl.2022.100004](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clpl.2022.100004), acquire the complete original and supplements, verify feed/study lineage and assess their own controls. Their metadata does not resolve the 2020 experiment.
4. Update only supported maintained claims, with canonical history and an independent exact-state review; otherwise retain these explicit limitations.

Primary retained artifacts: Robshaw2020 main PDF SHA256 `db9c50c8994aff7d6feffb3da1c7db0bd2a63ef8bae3ff3564a5a5bdedecb593`; SI SHA256 `df37acb92894b01da43f854646a234791ac42bba4ca2e1d042e4a5b4a53fa805`. Both came from White Rose Research Online record 157796. No author contact or paid access is requested. Existing issue #202 concerns a different waste-aluminium-electrolyte bioleaching original and remains separate.
title: Clarify Robshaw2020 spent-potlining recipe and recovery denominators

body:
Primary source: Chen et al. (2022), DOI [10.3390/ijerph19063465](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph19063465), complete original fourteen-page article and official PMC8955117 XML.

The qualified parasymplesite observation is supported by the labelled As-Fh diffraction trace in Figure 5d. Three source discrepancies limit stronger interpretation:

- Figure 5c places the approximately 29.35% solid-associated Fe(II) endpoint on squares and the approximately 12.30% endpoint on circles. Its caption maps squares to As-Ca-Fh and circles to As-Fh; the Abstract and Results 3.3 assign the higher proportion to As-Fh. Resolve the curve-to-arm mapping from an author correction or original labelled data before deriving a quantitative calcium effect.
- Methods 2.1 reports both a 5% bacterial suspension and 2 mL concentrated cells added to 200 mL medium. Resolve the inoculum volume/concentration used for these assays.
- Methods 2.6 describes cobalt radiation on a copper target. Obtain the actual XRD acquisition metadata before treating the radiation specification as resolved.

An acceptable follow-up would preserve the original conflicting statements, archive a legitimate published correction or author-deposited data/acquisition record, and update only the claims that the new evidence resolves. A private guess about swapped symbols is insufficient. The Fe(II) percentage is not a parasymplesite fraction or arsenic recovery yield. Matched sterile-solid diffraction, phase quantification and hydration remain separate experimental limitations.

This is a source-resolution issue, not a claim that the current narrow record is defective. The bounded correction search and current Crossref metadata did not identify a matching correction; that does not establish universal absence. All-state issue inventory (274 items in three retained API pages) was searched for the mineral, exact DOI and JH012 label without identifying an existing corresponding issue. No source contact was attempted.
title: Resolve Chen2022 parasymplesite experiment arm labels and reproducibility details

The new bismuthinite owner is grounded only in a complete abiotic primary (Carrasco-González et al.2024, DOI10.3390/ma17081818). It does not accept microbial synthesis from an abstract or a nominal Bi2S3 label.

Priority sources:

- Barton et al.2019, “Bismuth(III) interactions with Desulfovibrio desulfuricans: inhibition of cell energetics and nanocrystal formation of Bi2S3 and Bi0,” DOI10.1007/s10534-019-00213-4, PMID31549273. This was already deferred in round8 and screened again in round81. The round83 publisher PDF request returned subscription-page HTML; OpenAlex still exposes no open full-text location. That repeated request occurred before normalized-DOI dedup completed and provides no new scientific access.
- Kamaraj et al.2014, “Bio-assisted synthesis and characterization of nanostructured bismuth(III)sulphide using Clostridium acetobutylicum,” DOI10.1016/j.matchemphys.2013.11.042. The publisher abstract and truncated methods preview are accessible, but the downloaded route is denied HTML; OpenAlex has no open repository full text. The abstract reports orthorhombic phase and hexagonal morphology, which must not be conflated.
- Yue et al.2014, “Controllable extracellular biosynthesis of bismuth sulfide nanostructure by sulfate-reducing bacteria in water–oil two-phase system,” DOI10.1002/btpr.1894. This is also an existing round8 source gap. The current publisher response is challenge HTML; no complete original was acquired.

Acceptance requires legitimate complete originals and any associated SI; all relevant phase-identification graphics must be inspected, with crystallographic assignment distinguished from elemental composition or morphology. Record strain/consortium resolution, biomass state, substrate speciation, culture and processing conditions, cell-free/no-sulfate/no-bismuth/abiotic controls as actually provided, replication, and measured versus inferred outcome. Verify whether the phase supports bismuthinite specifically. Preserve negative controls and source inconsistencies; no recovery yield or industrial deployment may be inferred. A newly acquired source need not support an update. Do not close the whole acquisition issue on receiving only one source unless the remaining scopes are explicitly split or deferred.

Round83 bounded full issue-title/body inventory search found no exact overlapping source issue; prior research deferrals are retained and must remain linked. Source artifacts and exact access outcomes are in the round83 sulfides dossier and `/private/tmp/cmm-round83-sulfides-research`.
title: Acquire complete microbial Bi2S3 originals before assigning bismuthinite mechanisms

The independent review `20261014T225820Z-cuprite-round83-reference-provenance-initial` found a bounded provenance defect (minor, stable key `CMMMech.cuprite.reference-sequence-taiwan-provenance`).

In the draft `data/records/cuprite.yaml`, the U19043.1 evidence calls the historical reference “Taiwan provenance”; the accompanying source dossier calls it a “Taiwan source.” [GenBank U19043.1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/U19043.1) records a National Taiwan University submitting address in REFERENCE 2, but no specimen-country qualifier in FEATURES. A submitting institution does not establish biological collection origin.

Acceptance:

- Explicitly describe the Taiwan entry as the submission institution/address and leave specimen origin unresolved.
- Preserve the primary study's separate, unnamed UK lawn-soil experimental isolate and the reference-versus-isolate distinction.
- Correct the maintained owner and source assessment, append canonical EDIT history, and save an independent successor review with the stable issue key and exact predecessor occurrence.
- Validate the corrected bytes and verify the final review hash before merge.

This does not challenge the Cu2O culture observations or identify U19043.1 as the experimental isolate. No external source contact is needed.
title: Correct cuprite reference-sequence submission-address provenance

The final publication audit could not directly join four authority evidence rows in `20261014T231235Z-parasymplesite-round83-independent` to the archived files. The native review is schema-valid and the scientific claims are unchanged: snapshot hashes are optional. Exact source files, hashes and routes already exist in the round83 phosphate dossier.

Acceptance is a separate timestamped publication metadata addendum that binds the immutable review YAML hash and evidence IDs `handbook`, `ima`, `genbank` and `taxonomy` to the exact source paths, canonical URLs, versions and SHA-256 hashes. Verify each against the retained artifacts and dossier. Preserve the existing review, record and history bytes. The addendum must explicitly state that it supplies provenance metadata, not a new scientific verdict or a fresh acquisition.

Re-run the affected publication audit against the resulting package. No schema change, fabricated scientific finding, rewritten native review or new biological evidence is required.
title: Bind parasymplesite review authority references to archived artifacts
